# jumpcloud_system_group (Resource)

Manages a JumpCloud system (device) group.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Static system group
resource "jumpcloud_system_group" "production" {
  name        = "Production Servers"
  description = "All production systems"
}

# Dynamic system group (auto-populated based on OS)
resource "jumpcloud_system_group" "mac_devices" {
  name              = "Mac Devices"
  description       = "Automatically includes all macOS systems"
  membership_method = "DYNAMIC_AUTOMATED"

  member_query = jsonencode({
    queryType = "FilterQuery"
    filters = [
      {
        field    = "os"
        operator = "eq"
        value    = "Mac OS X"
      }
    ]
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the system group.

### Optional

- `description` (String) The description of the system group.
- `member_query` (String) JSON-encoded dynamic membership query. Required when membership_method is DYNAMIC_REVIEW_REQUIRED or DYNAMIC_AUTOMATED.
- `membership_method` (String) Membership method: STATIC, DYNAMIC_REVIEW_REQUIRED, or DYNAMIC_AUTOMATED.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the system group.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import jumpcloud_system_group.example <group-id>
```
